findings.where: js/three/lights.js:90 (scene-depth Discard) applied to the aureole term at :94-95; seen in E7 night_fog 28R approach (one of the spec §11.3 minimum-pass views)
findings.problem: Fog aureoles are clipped by every surface nearer than the light's own depth. Each ALS station's glow is therefore cut off at that station's screen row. Under the approach lights this produces a staircase of hard-edged horizontal glow bands. An aureole is forward scatter along the whole eye-to-light path, so geometry in front of the lamp should not cut it off. The same cut occurs at 0.6 NM.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/look2/look2_E7_nightfog_03nm.png, mean luminance of columns 300-340: 160->106 between rows 249 and 252, 105->72 between 261 and 264, 72->6 between 279 and 282 (one-row cuts). The band edges coincide with the ALS bar rows. The same bands appear in the next frame (tmp_look2_E7_nightfog_03nm_f1.png). /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/fix1/fix1_E7_nightfog_06nm.png columns 300-340: 118 -> 103/98 (row 244) -> 76/62/57 -> 0 at row 259 (single-row cut). Zoomed crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/envlook2/e7_crop.png, e7_crop_f1.png, e7f_crop.png. Probe: 174 aureoles drawn, slab fog 3-64 m, σ 0.0176.
findings.fix: Exempt the aureole from the per-pixel occlusion test, or attenuate it by the fog transmittance to the occluder (fraction of the scattering path in front of the surface) instead of discarding it. Keep the hard test for the core only.

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:343-349 fogInscatter (clearIn = skyEnvBlur at 2° above the view azimuth) used as the clear-air haze colour in fogNode; E3 dusk
findings.problem: In twilight, the aerial-perspective in-scatter of the clear air takes the radiance of the sunset horizon band (11-20 cd/m²). Near the ground the air is in the Earth's shadow (Sun -5.87°) and is lit only by skylight (~1 cd/m² mean). As a result the land, the airport and the hills render almost as bright as the sky behind them: no silhouette, and the floodlit airport and the ALS read as low-contrast smudges on tan haze.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/look2/look2_E3_dusk_28R_2nm.png (EV used 4.45, target 0.67). Hills rows 150-160 RGB (218,167,117), luminance 174, against the sky just above at (250,204,157), luminance 210 (display ratio 0.83, about 0.66 linear). Airport ground (179,135,98). Mean 164.6, p1 33. CPU mirror (scratchpad envlook2/haze.mjs, dusk_sky.mjs) at 5 km: haze (1-T 0.152) × the 2° sky ≈ 2.28 cd/m², against 0.17 cd/m² using the mean sky radiance (1.10 cd/m², cos-weighted, C171 GHI 3.44 lx) and 0.33 cd/m² for the concrete's own radiance. The haze is ~14× too bright and ~7× the surface's own radiance. Essentially unchanged from fix1 (mean 164.7). Only 40 local-maximum light points in the frame.
findings.fix: When the sun is below about -1°, blend the clear-air in-scatter colour toward the ambient (mean-sky) term, e.g. fogCol from skyUp, or toward a shadowed-air term weighted by the Earth-shadow height. Check that the hills read as dark against the sunset band.

findings.where: js/three/ground.js:611-612 (water envNode: sharp = sky.skyAlong(wp,Rr); blur uses cl = 0.2·sunColor+…); js/three/sky.js:175 (skyAlong composites only sky-shader layers, C.y>0.5, i.e. ≥5,000 ft); ground.js:599 (water body keeps mix(0.4,1,cloudShadow) of direct sun)
findings.problem: Under the low marine deck (OVC005 drawn as a plane), the bay mirrors the clear, sunlit, warm sky. The water band is the brightest element of the frame and is far brighter than the deck it should reflect, which breaks the spec E5 look ('flat grey OVC005 base, no sun'). At grazing incidence the water should be darker than the deck. The body colour also keeps 40 % of direct sun under a closed deck.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/look2/look2_E5_marine_tower.png: water band rows 102-114 (elevation -2.0° to -3.2°, 1.1-1.8 km NE of the tower) has luminance 190-209, RGB (213,206,197). The deck above, rows 0-90, has luminance 113-149 and the land 110-146. Probe: layers FEW003 and OVC005 (slab: true, own 1, threshold -2), planes 2, sun 'sun' with sunRad [13.4,10.9,7.75]. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/envlook2/e5_horizon.png. Reference /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/refs/cache/env_ref/sfo_fog_dusk_777_2012_960.jpg (CC BY 2.0) shows the water under an overcast deck as darker than the deck.
findings.fix: Include the slab (plane) layers in the reflected-sky composition (or ray-plane hit the low decks in skyAlong when ro is below them). Use the cloud-adjusted beam (sunVisibleP) in the blur term and the water body's sun term.

findings.where: E9 rain_day gate B26; js/three/ground.js:509-523 (wet film / puddles mirror only the PMREM env, no SSR); spec §7.6 (SSR on the high tier); renderer3 lamp reflections are night-only
findings.problem: In daylight rain the wet apron does not read as wet. There are no mirror images of the aircraft, bridge, stairs or GSE, and no sky sheen highlights. The puddles are still slightly darker blotches than the wet concrete around them (round-1 look1-3 is only partly fixed). The fix also made the apron much brighter and flatter than the step-3 render. The reference shows bright sky sheen and crisp object reflections as the main wet cue. SSR, which spec §7.6 asks for on the high tier, is not implemented.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/look2/look2_E9_rainday_gate_B26.png (wet film 1, pore 1, puddle 0.156, reflections 0, EV used 14.26 against target 13.49): near apron rows 300-360 have p5/p95 115/140 and std 9.4. The puddle blob at x185-205, y255-290 has luminance 136.8 against 143.7/145.3 for the wet surroundings. Image mean 167, p1 95.5, versus 133.7 / 66.5 in out/env/step3/env3_rain_day_gate.png. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/envlook2/e9_ground.png. Reference /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/refs/cache/env_ref/sfo_rain_day_t2_2011_960.jpg (CC BY 2.0, EV100 13.3) shows sky sheen and mirror images of stairs and GSE on the wet stand.
findings.fix: Add SSR (high tier) or a cheap planar or vertical-flip reflection of nearby objects on wet paved areas. Puddles should mirror the sky as the viewer sees it (including the mist in-scatter), not the deck seen from refPos. Re-check the A-WET criterion 'puddles mirror the sky' on a render.

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:491-494 (fog colour = fogInscatter + floodScatter only) together with the aureole occlusion in lights.js:90; E7 night_fog
findings.problem: Inside fog at night, objects near bright lamps render as crisp black cut-outs. The fog in-scatter colour contains only the floodlight field, not the aircraft or airfield lamps, and the lamps' aureoles are discarded over any nearer geometry. An aircraft ~50 m away in σ 0.0176 fog (T ≈ 0.41) should be veiled by its own landing-light glow, not be a black silhouette inside it.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/look2/look2_E7_nightfog_03nm.png: arriving aircraft about 50 m ahead (landing-light aureoles about 45 px radius). Engine pixels have luminance 0-1 and the fuselage 4, against 89-117 in the adjacent glow, a ratio of 0.01-0.04. The expected ratio is ≥ ~0.5 given T ≈ 0.41 and forward scatter in front of the body.
findings.fix: Draw the aureole (forward-scatter veil) over nearer geometry, scaled by the fraction of the path in front of it (see the critical finding), or add a screen-space lamp in-scatter term to the fog colour.

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:285-317 floodScatter (single scatter, at most 4 mean free paths after entering the lowest slab; multiple scattering not modelled); spec §11.2 E7 'flood domes on the apron'
findings.problem: From the approach above a shallow fog layer, there is no glow from the floodlit aprons under the fog. With σ 0.0176 the single-scatter samples (the first ≤227 m after entry) never reach the apron, so the fog top stays black. A 61-m fog layer of optical depth ~1.1 over 20-lx floods diffuses light to its top and glows (about 1-2 cd/m², visible at EV 4.6), so the domes named in the spec are missing.
findings.evidence: /home/user/Calc/sfo3d/out/env/fix1/fix1_E7_nightfog_06nm.png: 90 % of pixels black, and the only glow is the ALS aureole below the camera (the fixer's own probe: slab fog 3-64 m). In look2_E7 (camera inside the fog) the domes cannot be seen, as expected. Rough estimate of the fog-top glow: 20 lx × ~0.3 / π ≈ 2 cd/m², against 3 cd/m² mid-grey at the EV 4.6 night floor.
findings.fix: Add a cheap diffusion term: the fog-top or slab radiance above the flood field (e.g. the flood-field irradiance × an albedo-like factor × (1-e^-τslab), sampled where view rays cross the slab top). Verify it with a 0.6 NM render.

findings.where: js/three/rain.js:31 (AdditiveBlending) and renderer3.js:93/582 (RAIN_K × skyUp); E9 rain_day
findings.problem: In daylight, rain draws as bright white specks or dots, always brighter than the background (additive blending only). Against the bright overcast sky a drop shows roughly the mean of its surroundings, which is darker than the sky (the drop radiance model of Garg & Nayar, cited in the code). At 640×360 most streaks are 1-3 px, so the effect reads as snow.
findings.evidence: look2_E9_rainday_gate_B26.png: 1,757 local maxima with luminance more than 8 above the 7×7 median and none darker. Streak length 0.0877 m (v 5.26 m/s × 1/60 s), i.e. about 2 px at 20 m. 35,673 drops on the high tier.
findings.fix: Blend drops toward the environment mean (e.g. premultiplied 'over' with a radiance of skyUp×k + ground term) so they can be darker than the sky. Alternatively, lengthen the streaks for a 1/30 s display integration (a tagged choice).

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:433-466 cloudSlabMaterial and the scene fog; E5 marine_layer; exposure METER_BIAS (js/env/atmo/exposure.js:29)
findings.problem: The OVC005 base is perfectly uniform (threshold -2, so d≡1, no mottling) and it gets brighter toward the horizon. The CIE standard overcast sky has the opposite gradient: L ∝ (1+2 sin γ)/3, so the 9° part should be about 27 % brighter than near the horizon. The marine-layer exposure is still +1.65 EV above the §10 target, an already-open A-EXP failure.
findings.evidence: look2_E5_marine_tower.png deck rows 0→90: luminance 113→149 (darker high, brighter low). Metered EV100 14.3, used 13.62 against target 11.97. Reference sfo_fog_dusk_777_2012_960.jpg shows a mottled, structured stratus underside.
findings.fix: Add low-amplitude coverage noise to OVC slabs (d in 0.85-1) and an elevation-dependent base luminance following the CIE overcast law. Retune the meter bias for overcast (owner loop).

findings.where: js/three/flood.js:207-238 MastSpot (2 shadow-casting spots on high, 1 on low) and renderer3.js:688 _floodSpots; E4 night_clear gate
findings.problem: At night the parked A330's wing casts one long, sharp, near-black shadow across the floodlit stand. The single spot mast carries ~87 % of the local field, so the shadow has no fill from the other masts. Apron floodlighting is laid out so that a stand is lit from two or more directions to limit shadows (ICAO Annex 14 Vol I 5.3.24; quoted from memory, not re-checked).
findings.evidence: look2_E4_night_gate_B26.png row 260: apron luminance 66 → 8-10 inside the wing shadow → 61, a ratio of 0.13. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/envlook2/e4_shadow.png. Directional light is 'moon' (≈0.1 lx, too weak to cause this).
findings.fix: Cap one spot's share of the local field (or split it across the 2-3 nearest masts) so that shadows keep ≥40-50 % of the lit level. Soften the shadows by the lamp-array size.

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:302,308-311 (floodScatter N=6 per fogged fragment, N=8 for the background, a 3-D texture fetch each) and the aureole quads in lights.js (up to 2× a 5° radius); renderer3.js:284 tiers only horizN, slabs and layers
findings.problem: Tier behaviour: the new fog and flood in-scatter and the aureoles have the same per-pixel cost on the phone tier as on desktop. In fog with the floods on, every fogged pixel runs 6-8 extra 3-D texture samples with exp(), and up to ~170 aureole quads of ~100 px radius are blended additively. A-PERF has not been measured on any GPU.
findings.evidence: Code as cited. E7 probe: 174 aureoles drawn, landing-light aureole radius ≈45 px at 640×360 (≈5°, the cap), quad radius 2× that. No low-tier render was made in this round (5-render budget).
findings.fix: Tier the sample counts (e.g. low: 3/4) and cap the aureole quad radius or count on low. Measure on the owner's phone.

findings.where: js/three/sky.js:154-160 precompute (single scattering; ozone ×1.8 distributed like the Rayleigh profile; multiple-scattering stand-in 0.08·e^(45.8·sinEl) ≈ 7e-4 at -5.87°); E3 dusk
findings.problem: The civil-dusk sky has no blue in the 40° frame, and the modelled zenith is a weak pale blue. The twilight blue overhead is dominated by ozone (Chappuis band) absorption in the 20-30 km layer, which a sea-level-weighted ozone profile under-represents. The fixer lists this as open; the numbers are given here.
findings.evidence: look2_E3_dusk_28R_2nm.png top 20 % mean RGB (204,196,188), rows 20-40 % (245,223,196). CPU mirror (scratchpad envlook2/dusk_sky.mjs, k 0.321) toward the sun: 20° → 4.8 cd/m², RGB 1/.94/.92 (white); zenith 0.47 cd/m², .72/.75/1.0 (desaturated).
findings.fix: Give ozone its own layer (e.g. a tent profile centred at 25 km) in the precompute and the CPU mirror, then re-check the zenith colour at Sun -4° to -8°.

findings.where: js/live/app.js:193 (ownOf default 0.12) and :196 (base 1500 when no layer); old renderer §9.1 item 3
findings.problem: The old renderer draws a 12 % cloud layer at 1,500 m when the METAR reports no layer at or above 100 ft: CLR, SKC, or FG BKN000 only. Spec §9.1 item 3 asks for the reported layers only.
findings.evidence: look2_check.json old probe (live.html?wx=night_fog): R.env.cloud = [0.12, 1500, 14000, 0.5] with the METAR 'FG BKN000' and no layer ≥100 ft. The rain_day probe is correct: [0.704, 460.2, 4200] (BKN015, own 0.704).
findings.fix: With no layer, set the cover to 0.

findings.problem: The round-1 'dusk' reference photo is not a clear-dusk colour reference. EV100 2.66 at Sun 0.0° puts mid-grey at about 0.8 cd/m², roughly two orders of magnitude darker than a clear sunset sky, so the scene was under an overcast or fog deck (the title says fog) and its saturated blue may come from white balance. Judging the E3 sky colour against it would be misleading.
findings.evidence: EXIF in SOURCES.json: 1/5 s, f/4.5, ISO 1600 → EV100 2.66 → L_mid = 12.5·2^2.66/100 ≈ 0.79 cd/m². The model's clear sky at Sun 0° is about 10²-10³ cd/m² (CPU mirror). Added two openly licensed references this round: sfo_fog_dusk_777_2012_960.jpg (overcast deck) and sfo_rain_day_t2_2011_960.jpg (wet apron), both CC BY 2.0, recorded in SOURCES.json. A clear-sky dusk photo looking west at SFO is still missing (Commons API was rate-limited, 429).
findings.fix: Tag the 2016 photo 'overcast dusk' in SOURCES.json, and add or ask the owner for a clear civil-twilight photo looking west.

It finished with exit 0 at 18:19:06Z and nothing was re-rendered. live3 was ready in 7.5 s; buildings3d LOD2 took 760 s; the 5 views took 2,477 s. Per-view metering (EV100 metered → used vs target):
